newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish cabinet to debate airline sell-off Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Polish cabinet to debate airline sell-off Tuesday.

text.p: The Polish government will discuss the privatisation of the national air carrier PLL LOT SA on Tuesday, government spokeswoman Aleksandra Jakubowska said.
Jakubowska told a news briefing on Monday the government was likely to determine how many LOT shares would be retained by the treasury after the sell-off.
"The cabinet will also determine the procedure of selecting the official adviser on the sale," she said.

LOT, impatient with delays in privatisation which has dragged on since 1991, said on Friday it was considering strengthening its capital by floating between 10 and 15 percent of its shares in Poland or issuing convertible bonds abroad.
The company said it had plunged into the red last year but needed to continue expansion to keep apace with rising competition due to liberalisation of international flight regulations.

Last year the government, which has said it wants to sell a 49-percent stake of LOT, put off the deadline for the sale to June 30, 1998, from December 31, 1996, saying more studies on the complex process were needed.
The transport ministry had earlier annulled a tender for LOT's privatisation adviser, saying bidders had demanded excessively high fees.
